retro:
# Retrospective

## What worked
Bounded full-line policy reads from the first file; read-only security triage before launch; exact fresh model/native session verification; neutral public-only history; both finals saved before reading either. The narrow source comparison answers both author claims. Sol correctly declined generic extra testing. Coordinator evidence audit excluded overclaimed runtime results rather than laundering them through a valid seal.

## Friction and deviations
Initial git merge-base lookup preceded the explicit PR-object fetch and failed harmlessly; fetching head/original objects then pinned the comparison. An unsupported herdr guide discovery command failed, followed by documented --skill discovery; no lifecycle action preceded managed-context verification.
Opus's private stock adaptation removed cleanup but omitted transitive final-target assertions and gates, and retained only last-write inner streams. All C1-C6 execution claims are excluded, with original files and audit addendum retained. safety_process_compliant is false. There was no observed host configuration/service/hardware mutation. The correct public basis is source-only, not six-case validation.
Claude startup auto-memory loaded process-only reminders. No prior private technical conclusions were imported, but startup is not described as memory-free. Native transcripts are retained outside assignment by the harness. No intentional native-memory edits occurred.

## Correction
For future stock-test work, inventory AND implement every callee final-target assertion and immediate producer gate before running. Give each inner capture a distinct retained stream/status path. Merely removing EXIT cleanup or setting TMPDIR is insufficient. If source settles the narrow question, stop there rather than building unnecessary substitute experiments. Exact remediation is in PROCESS-DEVIATION.md and the reviewer's audit-addendum.md.

## Tools and cleanup
No confirmed tool bug or Omadev issue. Object-only source plus pinned blob inspection was sufficient. No desktop resources, servers or background test processes were used. Completed run receipts and reviewer attestations establish no owned runtime leftovers; no unrelated process enumeration or cleanup was attempted. Reviewer panes/history preserved for outer reset. HTML saved only, no publication by coordinator.
comment:
**Verified by source inspection:** Both points from the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12860#issuecomment-5776746054) are addressed at `4a004591c492`. No new issue was found in this scoped reassessment.

| Prior point | Resolution in the inspected revision |
| --- | --- |
| Pre-existing nounset failure in `omarchy-update-available` | The [initial comparison](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4a004591c492ab3e0a078c9db8b0f142c325c8f8/bin/omarchy-update-available#L9-L21) now uses `${OMARCHY_PATH:-/usr/share/omarchy}`. An unset variable skips the Git branch and reaches the package check. |
| Test-only loss of the Git logger in `update-dev-test.sh` | The [stripped-environment invocation](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/4a004591c492ab3e0a078c9db8b0f142c325c8f8/test/shell.d/update-dev-test.sh#L61-L72) now forwards `TEST_GIT_LOG`, connecting the Git stub to the file checked by the no-Git assertion. |

The added `update-available` regression case checks the unset-variable, no-package-updates outcome. That outcome correctly uses exit 1 with the up-to-date message, rather than treating every nonzero exit as a nounset failure.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Conclusions are based on pinned source and test-code inspection, not runtime validation. This follow-up does not establish full updater behavior, real package or Git operations, sudo/cron execution, or the desktop update indicator.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Opus 5.5 High and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical reviews, followed by Astra synthesis against the pinned source.
